rows.headline: India's money supply growth accelerates to 17.3%
rows.hook: Liquidity surge fuels inflation worries
rows.summary: Economist Steve Hanke reported that India's M3 money supply is growing at 17.3% annually. The six-month annualised growth rate reached 20.2%, while the three-month annualised rate surged to 31.5%. Hanke warned that this rapid expansion poses heightened risks of future inflation. Indian retail investors should monitor liquidity trends as excessive money supply can erode purchasing power and influence RBI interest rate decisions.
